frames.narration: Without reuse every request opens a connection. At 40 ms RTT, TCP costs one round trip and TLS 1.3 another: 80 ms before the request goes out. The request itself is 40 ms plus 20 ms of service, so the average is 140 ms. With TLS 1.2 it would be 180 ms.

With a pool the first burst still opens 32 connections (4 instances x 8), then they are reused. Requests cost 60 ms. The average over 6 bursts is 73 ms, and the 6 x 32 = 192 requests need only 32 connections.

Now traffic is sparse: a burst every 70 seconds. The load balancer drops connections idle for 60 seconds, but the client pool keeps them for 90. The pool hands out a connection the other side already closed.

The send fails: a reset arrives one round trip later (40 ms wasted), then the client must open a new connection (80 ms) and resend. 160 of 192 requests hit this, and the average rises to 173 ms, worse than never pooling.

Fix the order: client idle timeout 50 s, below the 60 s remote. The client now closes cleanly and opens a fresh connection each time, with no wasted send. Average 140 ms and 0 stale errors. The fix removes the errors, though not the setup cost: for that the traffic must be dense enough to reuse.

Pool size is multiplied by instance count. 40 instances each holding 8 connections want 320; the server accepts 100. Instances after about the first 12 are refused on every burst and 1,320 requests fail.

Cap the pool at 2 per instance: 40 x 2 = 80 connections, all served, 0 refused. The cost is queueing inside the instance: the 8-request burst needs 4 waves of 60 ms (240 ms on warm connections), and in the first burst the queue also waits 80 ms for the connection to open, so the maximum latency is 320 ms and the average 163 ms. Size from measured concurrency, not from fear.
